# Mt Buller winter warming vs the published Australian Alps rate

Winters at this station have not warmed in a way these records can show. Over 38 winters the change is close to nothing: for every ten years, somewhere between a cooling of 0.2 °C and a warming of 0.2 °C [fig 19].

## What it depends on

Each winter counts once, as the average of its June, July and August days. Four winters have few days on record; they are kept, and marked.

## What it does not mean

It does not show that the mountains are not warming. The slower of the published rates, 0.2 °C in ten years, still fits these records. The faster one, 0.36 °C, does not.

## How it was checked

Two ways of drawing the trend line were used, and they agree. The same was done for a second measure of cold, with the same result.
